results.title: Google introduces Stitch Loop to propose ongoing software fixes for human review | Superpower Daily
results.content:
The problem Google is targeting comes after the initial burst of building: maintaining security, improving performance and working out why users abandon parts of a product. In its introduction, Google pitches Loop to lean teams balancing that upkeep with new features. It describes the experiment as part of a new direction for Stitch, extending its ambitions from interface creation into continuous product improvement.

## From live signals to a proposed fix [...] Google Labs is testing Stitch Loop, an AI agent meant to keep improving software after launch—not just help build it in the first place. A team connects its GitHub code and gives Loop context about how the product is behaving, including signals like logs, user activity and feedback. It can draw on more than 180 integrations. The team then sets a measurable goal, such as improving checkout conversion. Loop looks for evidence of a problem and suggests possible fixes, including tradeoffs. A person chooses a direction; the agent writes the code in an isolated cloud sandbox and submits it as a GitHub pull request, with screenshots or video when useful. The intended cycle continues after that. Loop watches live product data and uses the results to shape its next suggestions. If a target is [...] ## Story brief

3 key points

Google Labs is testing Stitch Loop, a product-maintenance agent that turns live product signals and a team’s measurable goals into proposed software changes. It can keep tracking results and suggest follow-up work, but code changes remain ordinary GitHub pull requests that people must review before merging. The experiment broadens Stitch beyond interface creation toward ongoing product improvement; access starts through a global waitlist, with Google AI Ultra users prioritized.
